findings.finding: The primary Krea2EditModelPatch contract exposes VAE and source_image inputs for fit mode; the generated graph supplies both from the approved composite and Krea VAE.
The primary node documentation identifies 768 pixels as the grounded-encode default and describes the v1.2 trained range as 384–768; the generated graph locks grounding_px to 768.

The official ComfyUI Krea 2 documentation identifies Turbo as an eight-step distilled checkpoint and documents a 2 MP upper output range. The generated graph locks 8 steps, CFG 1, and an 832x1120 work canvas (0.93 MP).
The primary node documentation identifies v1.2 fit geometry and ref_boost as the reference-fidelity control; the generated graph supplies source_image and VAE to fit mode and locks ref_boost to 1.0.

The pinned ComfyUI revision 2a610155821d670a2d8047e654e5fce96b790eb5 exposes CLIPLoader with the krea2 type choice required by the primary Krea node contract. The live registry probe confirms the choice.

The pinned ComfyUI checkout and pinned comfyui-krea2edit checkout import on the local loopback server. All five API workflows match the live node registry, including Krea2EditModelPatch fit inputs, Krea2EditGroundedEncode inputs, and CLIPLoader type=krea2.

The required local qualification model files are present and SHA-256 verified by the model artifact preflight. This is an artifact inventory result, not proof that all weights can be resident or executed on the 16 GB Mac.

The private user fixture, approved local-copy-only background, model checksums, and preprocessing route passed. The first MPS attempt exposed the FP8 dtype limitation; the documented CPU-dequantization workaround then passed that exception site, but full-resolution and reduced diagnostic runs exhausted practical unified-memory/offload headroom before the first sampler step completed. Production generation remains fail-closed.

The official Comfy-Org Krea 2 NVFP4 artifact was downloaded and checksum-verified. It loaded through the live UNETLoader and reached KSampler, but the Apple-MPS run failed in the NVFP4 dequantization path with `Undefined type Float8_e4m3fn`. The locked artifact policy requires NVIDIA Blackwell SM>=10 for native NVFP4 compute, so this is not an approved Mac fallback.

A diagnostic CPU-only run using the checksum-verified official NVFP4 artifact, the exact human autoprompter instruction, the corrected foreground reference input, the immutable style LoRA, and the locked 832x1120 canvas completed all eight Turbo steps and exported a real candidate in 34:36. The run observed heavy swap and is not a production acceptance pass without two consecutive benchmark runs, calibrated thresholds, and an independent auditor PASS.

The current official Krea 2 inference source defaults its 12B pipeline to CUDA and does not expose a verified Apple staged-offload path for the required ComfyUI Identity Edit workflow. The official Turbo model card's generic MPS mention does not establish that capability.

compatibility_review.conclusion: Krea live core/node/schema compatibility and the project-owned FP8/MPS dtype workaround are verified in the pinned loopback runtime. The official lower-storage NVFP4 option is checksum-verified and fails the Apple-MPS capability path, while a separate CPU-only NVFP4 fallback completed the full human workflow and produced a real candidate at the locked canvas. A current official-source recheck found no approved Apple staged-offload route for the required ComfyUI Identity Edit workflow. This establishes execution capability but not production suitability: the default MPS route remains blocked, the CPU route is heavily swapping and has only one run, and the identity/style experiment matrix, calibrated thresholds, and independent audit remain blocked.
